title: Problem Overview and History
content: **Erdős Problem #718** asks: is there a constant C > 0 such that any graph on n vertices with ≥ Cr²n edges contains a subdivision of Kᵣ? A subdivision replaces each edge with a path. The question was answered YES independently by Komlós-Szemerédi and Bollobás-Thomason in 1996, dramatically improving Mader's 1967 exponential bound.
mathContext: This is a fundamental question in extremal graph theory about forced topological substructures.

title: Subdivision of Kᵣ
content: **IsSubdivisionOfKr** defines a subdivision of the complete graph Kᵣ: r branch vertices with paths connecting all pairs, where interior vertices are distinct from branch vertices. **ContainsSubdivisionOfKr** wraps this as a containment predicate.
mathContext: Also called a topological Kᵣ or TKᵣ. Subdivisions preserve the essential topological structure of a graph.

title: The Erdős-Hajnal-Mader Conjecture
content: **MaderConjecture**: there exists a universal constant C > 0 such that any graph on n vertices with at least Cr²n edges must contain a subdivision of Kᵣ. This conjectures a quadratic dependence on r, vastly improving the exponential bound.
mathContext: The quadratic bound is optimal up to the constant C.

title: Historical Results: Dirac and Mader
content: **dirac_1960**: 2n-2 edges forces a K₄ subdivision (initiated the field). **mader_1967**: 2^{r(r-1)/2} · n edges suffices for Kᵣ subdivision. This exponential bound stood for nearly 30 years before the quadratic improvement.
mathContext: These results established the systematic study of edge thresholds for topological cliques.

title: The 1996 Resolution
content: **komlos_szemeredi_1996** and **bollobas_thomason_1996**: Two independent proofs that the Mader Conjecture holds. Komlós-Szemerédi used extremal methods; Bollobás-Thomason used highly linked graph characterizations. **mader_conjecture_true** follows directly.
mathContext: One of the landmark results in extremal graph theory, proven independently by two groups in the same year.

title: k-Linked Graphs
content: **IsKLinked** (axiomatized): a graph is k-linked if any 2k terminals can be connected by k vertex-disjoint paths. **dense_graphs_linked**: graphs with Ckn edges are k-linked. This was a key lemma in Bollobás-Thomason's proof.
mathContext: A strong connectivity property related to subdivision existence, axiomatized since path-disjointness is complex to formalize.

title: Minors vs Subdivisions
content: **IsMinorOf** (axiomatized): H is a minor of G via edge/vertex deletion and contraction. **subdivision_implies_minor**: every subdivision gives a minor, but not conversely. Subdivisions preserve topological structure more strictly.
mathContext: The Graph Minor Theorem (Robertson-Seymour) is one of the deepest results in graph theory.

title: Main Results and Summary
content: **erdos_718_solved**: MaderConjecture is true (via Komlós-Szemerédi). **erdos_718_summary** and **erdos_718**: combine the quadratic bound with the earlier exponential bound, proved via exact ⟨komlos_szemeredi_1996, mader_1967⟩. The trivial True := trivial pattern has been replaced with a meaningful summary.
